chunks: Al-Tawhid: My father, from Sa'd, from Ibn Hashim and Ibn Abi al-Khattab and Ibn Yazid all together, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Udhayna, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Hunafa for Allah, not associating with Him,' and about Hanifiyya (the state of being Hanif). He said: It is the Fitra (innate nature) upon which Allah created the people, there is no change in the creation of Allah. He said: Allah created them upon Ma'rifa (Recognition/Knowledge).

Zurara said: And I asked him about the words of Allah: 'And when your Lord took from the children of Adam from their backs their descendants.' He said: He brought forth from the back of Adam his descendants until the Day of Judgment, and they came out like small particles, then He made them known to them and showed them His creation, and if it were not for that, no one would recognize his Lord.

And he said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Every newborn is born upon the Fitra,' meaning upon the Ma'rifa (Recognition) that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is his Creator. This is His words: 'And if you were to ask them, who created the heavens and the earth? They will surely say, Allah.'

key_terms.الْحَنِيفِيَّةِ: The state or quality of being a Hanif, pure monotheism.
key_terms.الْفِطْرَةِ: The innate, natural disposition or constitution with which humans are created.
key_terms.الْمَعْرِفَةِ: Recognition or gnosis, specifically the intuitive knowledge of God's existence and lordship.
key_terms.حُنَفَاءَ: Plural of Hanif, referring to those who are pure monotheists, inclining towards true faith.

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of Hanifiyya and Fitra in Shia theology regarding innate knowledge of God?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) defines Hanifiyya as the primordial Fitra of divine recognition (Ma'rifa), linking it to the cosmic event of extracting Adam's progeny to witness God's power. It establishes that innate knowledge of the Creator is inherent in human nature, supported by the Prophet's saying that every child is born upon this disposition. This concept is further validated by the Quranic assertion that humans naturally attribute creation to Allah when questioned.

en.ammaar-muslim: 8. [8/385] al-Tawhid: My father from Sa’d from Ibn Hashim, Ibn Abi al-Khattab and Ibn Yazid from Ibn Abi Umayr from Ibn Udhayna from Zurara from Abi Ja’far عليه السلام.

He (Zurara) said: I asked him about the words of Allah Mighty and Majestic: “Hunafa for Allah, not associating with Him (anything)” [22:31] and about the Hanifiyya (what is it)? He said: It is the Fitra which He created the people upon, there is no change in the creation of Allah. He (also) said: Allah created them upon the Ma’rifa (Recognition).

Zurara said: and I asked him about the words of Allah: “and when your Lord took from the children of Adam from their backs …” [7:172]. He said: He removed from the back of Adam his descendants up to the Day of Judgment, they came out like particles, then he made known to them and showed them His creation, and if it were not for that then no one would recognize (know) his Lord.

He (the Imam) also said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: “Every new born is born upon the Fitra”, that is, with the Ma’rifa (Recognition) that Allah Mighty and Majestic is his Creator. This then is His (Allah’s) words: “and if you were to ask them - who created the heavens and the earth - they will say Allah” [39:38]
